newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Fires rages through forests near Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Fires rages through forests near Jerusalem.

text.p: A forest fire raged in the foothills of Jerusalem on Friday, burning about 40 homes and large tracts of trees but causing no serious injuries, police said.
Flames whipped by high winds reached within 100 metres (yards) of the main Tel Aviv-Jerusalem highway on an extremely dry and hot day.
A police spokesman said 11 people were treated for smoke inhalation and helicopters and planes dropped water on the blaze. Dozens of fire engines and ambulances were at the scene.
Police ordered the evacuation of three agricultural villages, Kiryat Anavim, Maale Hahamisha and Beit Nakofa, and parts of the Jerusalem suburb of Mevasseret Zion.
The spokesman said some 40 homes were destroyed in Kiryat Anavim and Maale Hahamisha. Israel Radio reported the fire burnt 200 hectares (500 acres) of trees.

"Two communities were hit very hard by the fire. I am very happy to say that police carried out the evacuation very quickly so that hardly anyone was hurt," Jerusalem police chief Arye Amit told the radio.
The blaze, whose cause police said was still unknown, erupted about eight km (five miles) west of Jerusalem.
A little more than a year ago, a fire devastated pine forests along the western approaches to the city.
